currentFocus.title: Define browser/platform constraints for the Browser SQL target

stageSummary.planned: official capability research → target architecture → detailed planning → implementation decomposition → GitHub execution structure → final plan audit

baselineSource.result: V1 remains the frozen verified reference for browser collection, integrity, atomic persistence behavior, viewer recovery and browser runtime patterns.

planningBootstrap.result: Current responsibilities, reusable contracts, replaceable implementation choices, stale SQL planning and major unknowns were inventoried before target architecture design.

requirementsConsolidation.result: Existing product, decision and inherited-integrity requirements are classified without creating a duplicate authority; end-to-end acceptance behaviors and explicit non-goals are defined.
requirementsConsolidation.acceptanceCoverage: committed-cycle visibility, failed-cycle isolation, arbitrary SQL replacement, independent configurable cadence, 0..N results, query failure isolation, overrun/no-overlap, refresh/reopen, raw/null preservation, dynamic universe, temporal horizons, cross-security SQL and security boundary

architectureConstraint.rule: Browser SQL is fixed for this planning cycle. localhost/Node/.NET/native database paths are not active candidates or backlog items.

engineSelection.requiredNextEvidence: Define browser/platform constraints first, then verify official current capability documentation.

verification.specImpact: No runtime behavior changed. Phase B produced planning synthesis only; existing implementation specs remain baseline contracts until target Browser SQL design is complete.

next.action: Planning Phase C: define the browser/platform constraint matrix for Browser SQL.
steps: Define the target browser/platform scope (Chrome/Chromium on Windows) without selecting the SQL engine yet.
Map origin ownership and same-origin implications for the authenticated Leumi page, Viewer and browser persistence.
Identify CSP/CORS/module/Worker/WASM loading constraints that must be verified later rather than guessed.
Plan page/tab lifecycle, hidden/background throttling, persistence quota/eviction and security-boundary questions.
Classify each browser constraint as Verified, Inferred or Unknown and separate platform facts from engine-specific capability questions.
Do not start DuckDB-Wasm implementation or official engine capability research beyond what is necessary to define the constraint questions.

history.rule: Superseded architecture/research plans remain cold history and do not carry current progress.
